contexts.text: These three senses are circumstanced as was the tabernacle. Explained.
Three senses given. AC 4607. AC 4608. AC 4609.
Most things in the Word have two senses: a good sense, and a sense opposite to it. From their good sense is Known the quality of their opposite sense...
Whatever is written in the Word... is turned with the Angels into a corresponding sense, which sense does not at all appear in the sense of the letter...
These two senses are circumstanced as are the Internal and External with man.
The three senses of the Word. Explained. DSS 31. DSS 65. AR 725. TCR 777. AE 435:4. AE 630:2. AE 1024:2. AE 1083:2. AE 1083:8.
On the senses in the Divine Word. General article. WE 788. WE 4920. SE 1190. SE 2262. SE 2539. SE 5604.

All the commandments, like the rest of the Word, have two internal senses, besides the supreme, which is the third; one, which is proximate, and is called the spiritual moral sense; and another which is more remote, and is called the celestial spiritual sense.
On the four senses of the Word, See AE 1083:2. Example(s).
